newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 17.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:

* "Return of the Jedi: Special Edition" by News Corp's 20th Century Fox posted an estimated $16.3 million in sales its opening weekend, followed by Disney's "Jungle 2 Jungle" with sales of $11.3 million. "Private Parts" by Viacom's Paramount had sales of $9 million.
* Competition between direct broadcast satellites and cable operators promises to be a hotly-debated topic at this week's 1997 National Cable Television Association meeting.
* Billy Bob Thornton's Sling Blade and Joel Coen and Ethan Coen's Fargo won top honors at the Writers Guild of America Awards.
* Fred Zinnemann, the Oscar-winning director of "From Here to Eternity" and "A Man for All Seasons," died Friday in London at the age of 89.
* Time Warner Warner Bros.' "Selena" is one of very few Hollywood films targeting Hispanic audiences.
* Westinghouse's CBS is taking steps to reach a younger audience with shows like police drama "Brooklyn South" and "Family Matters."
